mcqs.question: A force of 10 N acts at 30° above the horizontal. What are its horizontal and vertical components?
mcqs.explanation: The horizontal component is F cosθ = 10 cos30° ≈ 8.66 N and the vertical component is F sinθ = 10 sin30° = 5 N. Option A gives these values; the other options mix the components or ignore the angle.

mcqs.question: A ball is thrown with a speed of 20 m/s at 45° above the horizontal. What are the horizontal and vertical components of the initial velocity?
mcqs.explanation: For a vector V, components are V cosθ and V sinθ. With V=20 m/s and θ=45°, both components equal 20 cos45° = 20 sin45° ≈ 14.14 m/s. The other options either ignore the angle or give incorrect magnitudes.

mcqs.question: A vector has components Fx = 6 N (east) and Fy = 8 N (north). Which of the following gives the correct magnitude of the vector?
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude = √(Fx²+Fy²) = √(6²+8²) = √(36+64) = √100 = 10 N. Adding the components (14 N) is a common mistake; the other numbers are unrelated.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: A force of 50 N pulls a block at 60° above the horizontal. A frictional force of 20 N opposes the motion horizontally. What is the net horizontal force on the block?
mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component of the pull = 50 cos60° = 25 N. Net horizontal = 25 N (pull) – 20 N (friction) = 5 N to the right. Options B and C ignore friction; D would imply friction exceeds the pull.

mcqs.question: Two forces each of magnitude 100 N act in the same plane. Force P makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal, and force Q makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal. Which force has the larger horizontal component?

options.D: Cannot be determined without more information

mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component = F cosθ. cos30° ≈ 0.866, cos60° = 0.5. Thus P’s horizontal component = 100 × 0.866 = 86.6 N, Q’s = 100 × 0.5 = 50 N. Therefore Force P has the larger horizontal component. The other options are incorrect.

mcqs.question: A vector of magnitude 25 N makes an angle of 120° measured counter‑clockwise from the positive x‑axis. What are its rectangular components (x, y)?
mcqs.explanation: x = 25 cos120° = 25 (‑0.5) = –12.5 N. y = 25 sin120° = 25 (√3/2) ≈ 21.65 N. Option A matches these values. The other options swap signs or coordinates.

mcqs.question: If a vector has components Ax = –3 m and Ay = 4 m, what is its magnitude?
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude = √( (‑3)² + 4² ) = √(9+16) = √25 = 5 m. The other numbers do not follow the Pythagorean relation.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: Why is it useful to resolve forces into perpendicular components when analyzing motion on an inclined plane?

options.A: Because components along and perpendicular to the plane can be treated independently
options.B: Because it changes the magnitude of the forces
options.C: Because it eliminates the need for friction

mcqs.answer: Because components along and perpendicular to the plane can be treated independently
mcqs.explanation: Resolving forces allows us to write separate equations for motion parallel and normal to the incline, simplifying the problem. The other statements are false: resolution does not alter magnitudes, does not remove friction, and vectors remain vectors.
